Issued at 220 AM EDT Sat Aug 29 2026

Today-Tonight...Broad mid-level ridging will remain situated 
across the Atlantic waters, with some troughing across north 
Florida continuing to weaken through today. At the surface, the 
Atlantic high is forecast to lift north of the Florida peninsula 
as a quasi- stationary boundary draped across the southeastern US 
weakens and washes out overnight. Locally, this set-up will keep 
east central Florida under a plume of deep moisture, with PWATs 
exceeding 2" areawide. Additionally, with the ridge axis shifting 
northward, the persistent southerly flow will finally shift, 
becoming more easterly both at the surface and gradually aloft. 
This will support development of the east coast sea breeze today, 
with the onshore flow assisting in its progression inland through 
this afternoon. Initial development of isolated showers and storms
along the sea breeze will be possible, with coverage anticipated 
to increase as the sea breeze pushes inland. The peak coverage 
will occur in association with the east and west coast sea breeze 
collision late this afternoon into the evening hours, primarily 
across Lake and western Orange and Osceola counties. Storm chances
will increase through the day as the environment becomes more 
favorable for development. Daytime heating will lead to increasing
instability across the area, with modest low-level lapse rates 
and MUCAPE of 1800 J/kg and greater forecast. Some drier air aloft
will help increase downdraft potential, with DCAPE forecast to 
range from 700- 1000 J/kg. Due to these parameters, the primary 
storm hazards for today will include frequent lightning strikes, 
wind gusts up to 55 mph, and heavy downpours. Minor, localized 
flooding cannot be ruled out in some spots, with quick rainfall 
accumulations of 1-3" possible. Shower and storm activity will 
diminish this evening following the sea breeze collision, with 
continued development across the local Atlantic waters forecast 
overnight. The persistent onshore flow may mean some activity 
makes it to the coast, but chances remain low (20-30%).

Temperatures today are forecast to reach the upper 80s to low 90s
along the coast and the low to mid 90s across the interior west 
of I- 95. While peak heat indices will remain below Heat Advisory 
criteria, values are still anticipated to range from 100F to 107F.
Adequate hydration, frequent breaks in the shade or A/C, and 
wearing lightweight, lightly colored clothing will all be 
important in order to prevent heat-related illness. Muggy 
conditions will persist into the overnight hours, though lows will
remain near normal in the low to mid 70s.

At the beaches, a moderate risk of rip currents is forecast due 
to a developing long-period swell and the onshore flow. Always 
swim near a lifeguard and never enter the ocean alone. Heed the 
advice of local beach safety officials and posted flags.

Sunday-Friday...Mid-level high pressure will slowly slide 
eastward across the southern US through the remainder of the 
weekend and into next week, where it is forecast to remain the 
predominant feature aloft over Florida. At the surface, broad high
pressure will remain in place, with the ridge axis staying north 
of the Florida peninsula. Locally, easterly winds both at the 
surface and aloft are anticipated to prevail, supporting 
development and intrusion inland of the east coast sea breeze each
afternoon. A moist air mass will remain in place across the 
peninsula with PWATs of 2.0-2.3" locally, keeping rain chances 
near to slightly above normal (40-80%). Activity will generally 
move towards the west coast, with an eventual sea breeze collision
across the interior leading to increasing coverage during the 
afternoon and evening hours each day. Storm development will be 
possible with this activity, with lightning strikes, gusty winds, 
and heavy downpours likely the primary concerns. Shower and storm 
activity will diminish into the overnight hours, though continued 
development across the local Atlantic waters cannot be ruled out 
each night along with a low chance for some light showers moving 
onto the coast due to the prevailing easterly flow. Outside of 
shower and storm chances, anticipate temperatures remaining 
generally near normal with highs in the upper 80s to low 90s and 
lows in the low to mid 70s. Humid and muggy conditions will 
persist, with a low chance of reaching Heat Advisory criteria in 
some spots late next week. Residents and visitors will be 
encouraged to remain adequately hydrated if spending extended 
periods of time outdoors and also take breaks in the shade or a 
building with A/C to help prevent the development of heat-related 
illness.
